description: Probe needed (read-only review cannot confirm by reading alone): if a caller populates `req.extra` with key "methodCalls" (or any other typed-field name like "using", "oldState", "queryState"), what does `serde_json::to_value(&req)` produce? Hypothesis: serde_json's flatten pass produces a JSON object with TWO "methodCalls" keys; downstream JSON parsers vary in which one wins, with no error signal. The non-flatten field is written first; the flatten extras append at the end. Test idea: pin behavior with a test that constructs JmapRequest, inserts methodCalls = ["acmeFake"] into extra, serializes, and asserts EITHER that serialization errors out OR that a documented winner is chosen. Currently no test exists. The doc comment on `extra` does not warn callers about this footgun. Fix: either (a) document the footgun explicitly in the rustdoc for every `extra` field, (b) add a debug_assert in a manual Serialize impl that rejects extras keys colliding with typed-field names, or (c) accept the footgun and document it once in the workspace policy. Repeats across 8 sites in jmap-types alone (GetResponse, ChangesResponse, SetResponse, SetError, QueryResponse, QueryChangesResponse, AddedItem, JmapRequest, JmapResponse) and is propagated by JMAP-lbdy.* to every extension type. This is a probe-deferred bead per the read-only review-myoss rule — do not write the probe in the tree from review.
title: Extras field can shadow typed fields on serialize, producing duplicate JSON keys
